implementation_plan.description: Verify the active git branch is 'feature/sound-effects-web-audio' (not main) before any code changes.

Add SoundEngine IIFE module to game.js immediately after the game-state variable declarations (after 'let scores = ...'). The IIFE captures private state (_ctx=null, _muted=false) via closure. It exposes: _ensureContext() for lazy AudioContext creation (checks window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext, resumes if suspended, returns null if neither exists); _hasContext() returning Boolean(_ctx) for test introspection; playClick() / playWin() / playDraw() / playNewGame() for the four synthesized sounds; toggleMute() and isMuted() for mute control. Each play method guards with 'if (_muted) return' before calling _ensureContext().

Define the four synthesized sounds inside SoundEngine using an internal hoisted helper function _playNote(ctx, frequency, type, startTime, duration, gainPeak): (1) playClick — 1 OscillatorNode, type='sine', frequency exponential ramp 600→150 Hz over 80 ms, GainNode from 0.3→0.001 in 80 ms; (2) playWin — 4-note ascending arpeggio: C5(523Hz), E5(659Hz), G5(784Hz), C6(1047Hz), type='sine', spaced 120 ms apart, each 150 ms, gain peak 0.25; (3) playDraw — 4-note descending minor: B4(494Hz), G4(392Hz), Eb4(311Hz), B3(247Hz), type='sawtooth', spaced 120 ms apart, each 180 ms, gain peak 0.18; (4) playNewGame — 1 OscillatorNode, type='sine', frequency exponential ramp 800→200 Hz over 300 ms, GainNode 0.15→0.001 in 300 ms.

Integrate sound calls into handleMove(): in the win-detected branch add 'SoundEngine.playWin();' just before the early return; in the draw-detected branch add 'SoundEngine.playDraw();' just before the early return; in the normal advance-turn path (after the draw check) add 'SoundEngine.playClick();' before switching currentPlayer. This ensures exactly one sound fires per successful move.
Integrate sound call into startNewGame(): append 'SoundEngine.playNewGame();' at the end of the function body, after all DOM updates (updateScoreCardHighlight() call).

Add 'let muteBtn;' to the DOM helpers block alongside the existing let declarations. In init(), add 'muteBtn = document.getElementById("muteBtn");' followed by a null-guarded event binding: 'if (muteBtn) { muteBtn.addEventListener("click", () => { const muted = SoundEngine.toggleMute(); muteBtn.textContent = muted ? "🔇" : "🔊"; muteBtn.setAttribute("aria-label", muted ? "Unmute sound" : "Mute sound"); muteBtn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(muted)); }); }'. The null guard ensures existing test fixtures that omit #muteBtn do not throw.
Export SoundEngine via module.exports at the bottom of game.js. Add 'SoundEngine,' to the existing exported object so Jest tests can call toggleMute(), isMuted(), and _hasContext() directly.

Add the mute toggle button to index.html's .controls div, after the Reset Score button: '<button class="btn btn-ghost btn-icon" id="muteBtn" type="button" aria-label="Mute sound" aria-pressed="false">🔊</button>'. Uses aria-pressed to communicate toggle state to screen-reader users.

Add '.btn-icon' CSS rule to index.html's <style> block just before the '/* Responsive Tweaks */' section: '.btn-icon { padding: 0.55rem 0.8rem; font-size: 1.2rem; line-height: 1; }'. This gives the emoji icon correct sizing without overriding .btn-ghost visual styles.

Create __tests__/game.sound.test.js. Use the jest.resetModules() + require() pattern (matching game.coverage.test.js) so Jest coverage instrumentation covers the new SoundEngine code and each test gets a fresh module instance (_ctx=null, _muted=false). Set global.AudioContext = MockAudioContext before each require('../game.js'). The GAME_HTML fixture in this file mirrors game.coverage.test.js but adds the #muteBtn element to .controls.
Run the full Jest test suite (npm test) to confirm all pre-existing tests still pass and all new sound tests pass. Address any failures before committing.
Commit all changes on the feature branch with a descriptive message covering the SoundEngine implementation, mute button, and test coverage. Do NOT merge to main.

new_files.purpose:
Jest unit test suite for the SoundEngine module and its integration into game events. Organized into four describe blocks:

(1) 'SoundEngine — lazy AudioContext initialization'
- AudioContext constructor NOT called on module load
- AudioContext NOT called after DOMContentLoaded fires alone (no user gesture)
- AudioContext IS called after the first sound-producing action (handleMove)
- game.SoundEngine._hasContext() used for precise assertions

(2) 'SoundEngine — sounds triggered on correct game events'
- Normal move calls createOscillator (playClick: 1 oscillator)
- Winning move triggers playWin (4 oscillators, ascending arpeggio)
- Draw-completing move triggers playDraw (4 oscillators, descending minor)
- startNewGame() triggers playNewGame (1 oscillator, whoosh)
- handleMove on taken cell is a no-op (no extra oscillators)

(3) 'SoundEngine — mute suppresses audio output'
- toggleMute() prevents createOscillator calls on subsequent moves
- Win sound suppressed when muted
- Draw sound suppressed when muted
- playNewGame suppressed when muted
- Double-toggle restores unmuted state and sound resumes
- toggleMute() return values (true when muting, false when unmuting)
- isMuted() state accurately reflects current setting

(4) 'Mute button DOM integration'
- Clicking #muteBtn sets isMuted() true and textContent to '🔇'
- aria-pressed becomes 'true' and aria-label becomes 'Unmute sound'
- Second click restores textContent to '🔊', aria-pressed to 'false'
- aria-label restores to 'Mute sound' after second click

(5) 'SoundEngine — edge cases'
- No throw when AudioContext is unavailable (global.AudioContext = undefined)
- webkitAudioContext fallback used when AudioContext undefined but webkitAudioContext defined
- AudioContext.resume() called when ctx.state is 'suspended'
- No throw when #muteBtn absent from DOM (null guard in init)

Test infrastructure: Each test uses jest.resetModules() + setupAudioContextMock() before require('../game.js') to get a fresh module. MockAudioContext returns a mock ctx with jest.fn() stubs on createOscillator, createGain, currentTime=0, state='running', resume. The GAME_HTML fixture includes #muteBtn in .controls.

test_plan: AudioContext is NOT instantiated when game.js module is loaded via require() — SoundEngine._hasContext() === false before DOMContentLoaded
AudioContext is NOT instantiated after DOMContentLoaded fires (init() runs but no sound called) — _hasContext() still false
AudioContext IS instantiated on the first call to a play* method — after handleMove(0), _hasContext() === true and MockAudioContext called exactly once
AudioContext.resume() is called when _ctx.state === 'suspended' — mock ctx.state set to 'suspended', playClick triggered, verify ctx.resume was called
playClick fires on a successful non-terminal move — handleMove(0) increases createOscillator call count by exactly 1
playWin fires on the move that completes a win — sequence X:0,1 O:3,4 then handleMove(2); createOscillator count increases by 4 (not 1); playClick not additionally called
playDraw fires on the draw-completing move — use _setState to pre-load board one move from draw, then handleMove; createOscillator count increases by 4
playNewGame fires when startNewGame() called — after one move to initialize ctx, call startNewGame(); createOscillator count increases by 1
handleMove on a taken cell is a no-op — place X on cell 0, call handleMove(0) again; createOscillator count does not increase on second call
handleMove after gameOver is a no-op — after X wins, call handleMove on empty cell; no additional createOscillator calls
Muting via SoundEngine.toggleMute() suppresses playClick — move after mute produces zero new createOscillator calls
Muting suppresses playWin — mute, then complete a win; createOscillator not called for win
Muting suppresses playDraw — mute, then complete a draw; createOscillator not called
Muting suppresses playNewGame — mute, call startNewGame(); createOscillator not called
toggleMute() returns true when called from unmuted state
toggleMute() returns false when called from muted state
isMuted() reflects current state: false initially, true after one toggle, false after double-toggle
Sound resumes after unmuting — move while muted: no oscillator; toggle unmute; next move: oscillator called again
Clicking #muteBtn sets isMuted() to true and muteBtn.textContent to '🔇'
Clicking #muteBtn sets aria-pressed='true' and aria-label='Unmute sound'
Clicking #muteBtn a second time sets isMuted() to false and muteBtn.textContent to '🔊'
Clicking #muteBtn a second time sets aria-pressed='false' and aria-label='Mute sound'
init() does not throw when #muteBtn is absent from the DOM (null-guard protects addEventListener call)
No error thrown when AudioContext is unavailable (global.AudioContext = undefined, global.webkitAudioContext = undefined) — handleMove called, no throw, createOscillator never called

webkitAudioContext fallback used when window.AudioContext is undefined but window.webkitAudioContext is defined — MockAudioContext assigned to webkitAudioContext, handleMove called, MockAudioContext called once

All pre-existing Jest tests in game.dom.test.js, game.coverage.test.js, game.logic.test.js, game.exported-api.test.js, game.checkwinner-switcher.test.js, css-animations.test.js, keyboard-accessibility.test.js continue to pass without modification
rollback_plan:
Because all work is isolated to the feature branch 'feature/sound-effects-web-audio', rollback options are graduated by severity:

1. PARTIAL ROLLBACK (revert a single bad commit): `git revert <commit-sha>` on the feature branch — creates a new commit that undoes specific changes while preserving history.

2. FULL FEATURE ROLLBACK (abandon the branch without touching main): switch back to main with `git checkout main`. The feature branch is discarded locally with `git branch -D feature/sound-effects-web-audio`. Since main is never touched during development, it remains at the last stable state.

3. POST-MERGE ROLLBACK (if the branch was already merged to main via PR): `git revert -m 1 <merge-commit-sha>` reverts all feature changes in a single commit, safe for shared history.

4. MINIMAL IN-PLACE DISABLE (emergency, no git required): In game.js, replace the SoundEngine IIFE body with a stub: `const SoundEngine = { playClick(){}, playWin(){}, playDraw(){}, playNewGame(){}, toggleMute(){ return false; }, isMuted(){ return false; }, _hasContext(){ return false; } };`. This silences all audio instantly without removing the call sites, leaving the rest of the game fully functional.

No database migrations, server changes, or new external dependencies are introduced, making rollback straightforward at any stage.
